cells.tense: The clearing has happened, and you're here with what remains, growing it on purpose.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: Water it, repair it, make the call — whichever comes next — where the person it's for can watch you do it. Once. No announcement after.
cells.core:
A structure you were leaning on came down — a plan, an arrangement, a version of things that stopped holding — and what's left is open ground. You know what to do with open ground. You work by hand: how much water, how much patience, when to leave well enough alone, at the rate the thing itself can go.

One piece of that care, done where it can be seen, is the balance here. Not announced, not performed — the watering, the repair, the call, with the light on. What has been kept private gets air, and the person it's for watches it happen. It costs the comfort of going unobserved. The work stops being something only you know about.
cells.sheetLine: You grow what's in your care, by hand, at the rate it can go.
cells.verb: Growing what's in your care, by hand, at the rate it can actually go.
cells.place: A clearing — the false structure just came down; what remains is open and unfinished.

cells.tense: The clearing is over, and you're already growing the next thing — reaching past what's actually here.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Take something already finished — done, here, yours — and be full with it for one hour. No next version. Eat the meal and leave the kitchen.
cells.core:
When something ends or comes apart, you move outward fast — to the next patch of ground, the next thing to grow. There's a clearing in your life right now that's barely been walked, and you're already planting in it. Your gift for growing things is pushing past the moment it was for. Care ahead of need starts to look like control, and the people standing in that ground can feel it.

So take one finished thing, small and real, and be full with it for an hour. The meal you cooked, the thing you built, the version that's already here. Savoring what exists takes the pressure off what's next, and the next round of work runs cleaner for it. What you give up is the reach. What you get back is ground you can stand on.

cells.verb: Growing what's in your care, by hand, at the rate it can actually go.

cells.tense: The clearing happened, and you're still at the edge of it, not yet walking in.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Return to a patch you were growing for yourself — nobody else's — and give it an hour this week. Not a restart. An hour.
cells.core:
Something came down — a structure, an arrangement, a plan — and you're at the edge of what's left, not yet walking in. Your care for growing things is real; it just isn't pointed at anything right now. Care with no garden gets heavy. You've been carrying what you used to grow instead of the growing itself, and the patch where it lived is still there, still yours.

This isn't a push to try harder — effort aimed at bare ground just wears it thinner. The ask is an hour in the patch that was yours before everything else took the front row. Not for anyone, not measured by anyone. Not a restart, not a plan. That's how the following gets done after everything: an hour, this week, and the patch is walked again.
cells.sheetLine: The patch is still yours, and it has been waiting.

cells.tense: You are holding something together for someone right now and would not call it that.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: When you quietly cover for someone — the fixing, the slowing down, the thing you absorb so they don't — let the cost show once. Say nothing about it after.
cells.core:
You keep a lot standing for other people. Not with drama — with small, steady care that has no witness and no ceremony. The work is real. What you'd say if asked is that you helped out, that you covered for someone, that you don't make a fuss. This labor is yours; the account of it got left off the page.

What's hard to see is a sacrifice you don't count as one. Letting it be seen once — the steadying you do where the person it's for can watch you do it — isn't asking for a parade. It gives the thing air, and lets them know what was given. Ease comes after the showing, not before. One moment, no explanation attached to it.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what you don't call holding, and the cost goes unseen.

attempts.check: The one bumpy claim: I render the Too Much status as cultivating ahead of the clearing — someone still tending a structure the truth has already made false. The record's Too Much face (over-expressing, pushing ahead of natural timing) supports this, but a reader could say the clearing already happened and they're just holding ground. If that's true, the Fulfillment ask still lands — being full with what's already here costs nothing and teaches something either way. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'You are tending a garden the ground has already moved under' — it's pretty, so it stays out. I fixed that by making the core describe the tending-in-the-open rather than the metaphor.
